key_insight: The paper shows that a frozen large language model can teach a domain-specific molecular generator to follow high-level natural-language discovery goals, even when the target space is initially poorly covered.
clinical_relevance: This could help accelerate early-stage cancer therapeutic discovery by steering peptide and small-molecule generators toward candidate designs with desired bioactivity, though it remains a preclinical research approach.
method: LLM sets adaptive intermediate sub-goals based on the generator's current capabilities
The model judges sampled candidates under each objective and turns those judgments into preferences
Preferences are distilled into the generator with DPO to iteratively align outputs to the final goal
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on therapeutic peptides and small-molecule design, showing improved goal-directed control toward natural-language discovery tasks.
watch_item: Performance depends on the LLM's judgments and on reliable experimental priors, so weak proxy reasoning or mismatched objectives could steer the generator toward misleading candidates.
paper_title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
